mining_tax_base: other (royalty on gross sales at a rate set by EBIT margin; marginal 8% of EBIT)
formula: Gold formula tax = (34 - 170/x)% x TI, x = 100 x TI / gold revenue, so tax = 0.34 TI - 0.017 Rev (marginal 34%). Royalty = Sales x (0.5 + EBIT/(Sales x 12.5) x 100)% = 0.005 Sales + 0.08 EBIT (marginal 8% of EBIT below the 5% cap). Combined marginal = 0.08 + (1 - 0.08) x 0.34, assuming royalty deductible for income tax
source: SARS, Guide for Tax Rates/Duties/Levies, Issue 15 (17 Feb 2022, archived); Mineral and Petroleum Resources Royalty Act 28 of 2008 ss. 3, 4, Schedule 1 (lawlibrary.org.za consolidation)
source_location: SARS guide s. 1.1 (company rate 28%), s. 1.2.1(a) (gold formula Y = 34 - 170/x for years ending 1 Apr 2012 to 31 Mar 2021); Royalty Act s. 4(1), 4(3), Sch. 1 (gold refined)
note: Gold mining income is taxed by formula, not at the 28% company rate: average rate 34 - 170/x (e.g. 28.3% at a 30% taxable-income margin) but marginal rate 34% on taxable income. The pre-2012 alternative formula (43 - 215/x for STC-exempt companies) no longer applies from 2012. The Mineral and Petroleum Resources Royalty is levied on gross sales but its rate rises with EBIT margin, so 8% of each extra rand of EBIT is royalty until the 5% cap (EBIT margin 56.25%); it is included here as a profit-linked component with base 'other'. Excluding it, the combined marginal rate is 34%. Royalty deductibility for income tax not confirmed in the sources consulted. Formula confirmed in the SARS guide for years ending to 31 Mar 2021; later months of 2021 assumed unchanged.
